plain_english: Katherine Glasgow is identified as the spouse of Thomas Weir in Stevenston parish. The opening gives her death in January 1603, not on the subsequent probate date. Thomas supplied the account on behalf of William, James and probably Jonet Weir; the confirmation refers to the executors’ minority. This does not by itself explicitly state their parentage.

The estate inventory includes horses, cattle, oats and household or personal belongings. There are no debts owing into the estate. Outgoing obligations include rent, a payment connected with the minister at Stevenston and servants’ fees. The debts exceed the assets. Unread sums and creditor names must not be treated as a completed financial or kinship reconstruction.
The confirmation states “the nynt day of may 1605”: 9 May 1605. This fresh reading resolves the previous apparent disagreement with the printed calendar and Findmypast index.
findings: Image 6, opening lines 3–7: spouse Thomas Weir, Stevenston parish and January 1603 death are directly supported.
Image 7, confirmation line 1: “the nynt day of may 1605” supports 9 May 1605. The prior [26?]/[xxvj?] reading is superseded.

Image 6 opening and image 7 confirmation: the named representatives/executors and minority do not constitute an explicit statement that all three were the couple’s children. That proposed relationship remains an inference.
Image 7 accounting section: household goods, external obligations and servants’ wages are estate evidence, not evidence that creditors or cautioners were relatives.
changes_from_previous: Expanded the former three-line selection into a working reading of opening, inventory, debts and confirmation across both supplied pages.
Corrected disputed [26?] May confirmation to 9 May from the written ordinal nynt, independently of the index.
Separated neighboring estates from Katherine’s entry. Retained rather than silently overwrote the preceding selective review in previous_selective_review.
Did not carry uncertain creditor surnames, monetary totals or the commissary’s full name from the earlier polished transcript into fresh literal readings.
unresolved: Several inventory quantities, prices and names remain undeciphered.
Jonet’s forename remains qualified; no clear parent-child term was recovered in the washed opening continuation.
Readability of the commission and cautioner’s full name remains insufficient for an independent fresh transcription of every word.
